g.text: 1.1 Business Model — How Nikharta Roop Earns Money
Nikharta Roop is a multi-channel beauty parlour business that operates both through
physical walk-in customers and a digital booking platform. The platform enables
customers to discover services, book appointments, and leave reviews — all in Hindi.
Customers pay for beauty services (haircut, facial, bridal makeup)
10–20% advance collected during online booking to prevent no-shows
Combo packages at discounted rates to increase order value
Festival discounts (Diwali, Eid, Navratri) drive volume
Repeat customers earn points redeemable on next visit
Franchise or company-owned branches in multiple cities
Beauty products sold at parlour or via app
Understanding our users is critical for building the right features. Below are four
real-world personas representing our core audience.
Quick haircut or threading before college event
Book facial on weekend without going in person
No time to call, uncertain slot availability
Book complete bridal package months in advance
Wants to compare packages, scared of last-minute cancellation
Book monthly facial or hair spa nearby
Prefers Hindi UI, not comfortable with English apps
Manage daily bookings, staff, and services
Overwhelmed by phone calls, no cancellation visibility
Journey A: First-Time User Flow (New Customer — Priya)
• Priya searches 'beauty parlour near me' on Google → lands on Nikharta Roop website.
• She sees the Home page in Hindi with services listed and an attractive banner.
• She clicks 'Services' → browses 'Threading' under 'Face Care' category.
• She clicks 'Book Now' → prompted to login. She enters her mobile number.
• OTP received via SMS → she enters it → account auto-created.
• She selects date, time slot, and preferred staff (optional).
• She sees the summary: Service + Price + Time → pays ₹50 advance via UPI.
• Booking Confirmed screen appears. WhatsApp message received instantly.
• Day of appointment: she receives a reminder SMS 2 hours before.
• Post-service: she receives a link to leave a review.
Journey B: Repeat Customer Flow (Sunita — Working Woman)
• Sunita opens the Nikharta Roop app on Sunday morning.
• She is already logged in (token saved). Home page shows her last service.
• She taps 'Book Again' on her previous 'Facial' service — date picker opens.
• She selects next Saturday, 11 AM slot — sees it's available.
• She confirms booking — no payment needed (loyalty discount applied).
• Kavita opens the website on her laptop 3 months before wedding.
• She navigates to 'Bridal Packages' category — sees detailed package cards.
• She reads descriptions, views photo gallery of previous work.
• She books a 'Pre-Bridal Consultation' slot first (free) to discuss requirements.
• Admin confirms the consultation booking via Admin Panel.
• After consultation, admin creates a custom bridal package for Kavita.
• Kavita receives WhatsApp with full package breakdown and payment link.
• She pays 30% advance — booking is locked.

g.text: The Nikharta Roop platform is built on a three-tier architecture: Presentation Layer
(UI), Application Layer (API & Business Logic), and Data Layer (Database & Storage).
All layers are separated to allow independent scaling.
Android + iOS app from single codebase
OTP storage, session tokens, slot availability cache
Service images, staff photos, portfolio images
UPI, cards, net banking for advance payment
Below is the exact sequence of events from when a user taps 'Book Now' to when the
Validates form inputs locally (date, slot selected)
Sends POST /api/bookings with auth token + booking data
Validates JWT token, checks user permissions
Checks slot availability in DB, prevents double-booking
Creates booking record with status = PENDING
Initiates Razorpay payment order if advance required
Returns booking ID + payment URL to app
Completes UPI payment inside Razorpay checkout
Sends WhatsApp + SMS confirmation to user
Polling or WebSocket detects confirmation → shows success screen
Renders pages, collects user input, calls APIs, shows results
Validates data, applies rules (slot conflict, RBAC), orchestrates DB calls
Never stores files or serves static assets directly
Persists data, handles relationships, indexes for fast queries
Never applies business rules or talks to external APIs
• Images lazy-loaded with next-gen formats (WebP) — saves 30–50% bandwidth.
• API responses paginated — never load more than 20 records at once.
• App caches service list locally (refreshed every 24 hours) for offline browsing.
• OTP retry logic with 30-second cool-down to avoid SMS cost waste.
• React Native uses FlatList (virtualized) for long booking history lists.
• WhatsApp preferred over email — 90% of users already have it installed.

g.text: Indian mobile users are not comfortable remembering passwords. OTP via SMS is the most
trusted and widely used authentication method in India, used by PhonePe, Paytm,
Swiggy, and every major Indian app. It also eliminates the risk of users forgetting
Generates 6-digit OTP, stores in Redis with 5-minute expiry
Calls MSG91 API to send OTP SMS
Client sends mobile + OTP to POST /auth/verify-otp
Compares OTP with Redis value, checks expiry
Queries Users table for this mobile number
Creates new User record with mobile, assigns USER role
JWT contains: userId, role, mobile, expiry (7 days)
Returns user profile + JWT token to app
Deletes OTP from Redis to prevent reuse
JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, self-contained token that carries user identity
without hitting the database on every request. It has three parts: Header, Payload,
Used for RBAC checks on every API
Which branch this staff/admin belongs to
Issued At — when the token was created
Expiry time — after this, token is invalid
• User logs in → JWT token created with 7-day expiry.
• App stores token in secure storage (Keychain on iOS, EncryptedSharedPreferences on
• Every API call includes the token in Authorization header: Bearer <token>.
• API middleware decodes the token and reads userId + role.
• If token is expired → API returns 401 Unauthorized → app redirects to login page.
• User can manually logout → app deletes token from local storage.
• Admin can invalidate all tokens for a user (e.g., if account is suspended).
Redis key expired → OTP not found → reject
'OTP की समय-सीमा समाप्त हो गई। दोबारा भेजें।'
Mismatch in Redis → reject, increment attempt counter
Lock the mobile number for 15 minutes in Redis
'बहुत अधिक प्रयास। 15 मिनट बाद पुनः प्रयास करें।'
Provide 'Resend OTP' button — available after 30 seconds
'OTP नहीं मिला? 30 सेकंड बाद दोबारा भेजें।'
Both can have valid tokens simultaneously (allowed)

g.text: Over 85% of Nikharta Roop's users will access the app on Android smartphones with
screen widths of 360–414px. The design starts with mobile layout and expands to
• Minimum touch target size: 44x44px for all buttons and interactive elements.
• Bottom navigation bar on mobile (not hamburger menu) — thumb-friendly.
• Single-column layouts on mobile, two-column on tablet, three-column on desktop.
• Critical actions (Book Now, Pay, Confirm) are sticky at the bottom of the screen on
• Forms use native mobile keyboards — numeric keyboard for phone/OTP, text for names.
Buttons, links, active states, brand elements
Headings, important text emphasis, hover states
Available slots, confirmed status, success messages
App background — easier on eyes than pure white
All Hindi UI text — optimized for Indian scripts
12px for cards, 8px for buttons, 50% for avatars
• All primary labels, service names, and button text must be in Hindi first.
• Hindi text requires 20–30% more horizontal space than English — factor into
• Use simple, conversational Hindi — avoid formal/bureaucratic language.
• Example: Use 'अभी बुक करें' (Book Now) not 'नियुक्ति अनुसूचित करें' (Schedule
• Date and time display: use Indian format — 'शनिवार, 15 दिसंबर 2024, दोपहर 11 बजे'.
• Currency display: '₹ 500' with Rupee symbol — never 'INR 500'.
• Placeholder text in forms: in Hindi — 'अपना नाम यहाँ लिखें'.
• Error and success messages: always in Hindi — users trust Hindi over English.

g.font-family: Noto Sans Devanagari, Inter, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: The parlour operates in 30-minute time slots. Each slot is generated dynamically based
on branch opening hours and service duration. The system never hard-codes slots in the
Last appointment must END by 8 PM
Users cannot book more than 2 months in advance
Cannot book a slot starting within 2 hours
User can cancel up to 2 hours before the appointment
9.2 Slot Availability Logic — Step by Step
When a user selects a service and a date, the system runs this process to determine
• Calculate all possible slots for the day: 09:00, 09:30, 10:00 ... 19:30 (last slot
• Filter slots that are in the past or within the 2-hour minimum advance window.
• Query Bookings table: find all CONFIRMED or PENDING bookings for the selected date,
branch, and staff (if staff is selected).
• For each booked slot, mark the time range as UNAVAILABLE (including service
duration — a 60-min service at 10:00 blocks 10:00 AND 10:30).
• If staff_id is provided: only check that staff member's bookings. If no staff
selected: check parlour-level capacity (total staff available for that slot).
• Return remaining AVAILABLE slots to the user as a visual grid.
✅ Example: User wants a Facial (60 min) on Saturday. Slots 10:00 and 11:00 are already
booked by two different customers. So the 10:00 slot appears RED (unavailable). But
User selects a specific staff member
System checks ONLY that staff member's availability. If she's busy, that slot shows as
System finds all staff qualified for the service and checks if at least one is free in
System assigns the staff member with fewest bookings that day (load balancing). Stored
Admin marks staff as unavailable. System reassigns all their future bookings to
Only staff with the service in their specializations array appear as options for that
Immediately after user submits booking (awaiting payment)
When customer arrives and admin checks them in
After service is done, marked by admin or staff
By user (2 hrs before) or by admin anytime
User did not show up, admin marks after appointment time
A race condition occurs when two users try to book the same slot at exactly the same
time. The system prevents double-booking using database-level locking.
• Step 1: When a booking is submitted, the API starts a database transaction.
• Step 2: It does a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the relevant time slot row — this locks
• Step 3: If another request tries to book the same slot simultaneously, it waits.
• Step 4: First request succeeds → booking created → lock released.
• Step 5: Second request runs → sees slot is now taken → returns 409 Conflict.
• Step 6: User who lost the race gets: 'माफ़ करें, यह स्लॉट अभी भर गया। कोई दूसरा समय
⚠️ Edge Case: User holds a slot in the booking form for 10 minutes without completing
payment. System should hold a PENDING booking for maximum 15 minutes, then auto-expire
it, releasing the slot back to available.

g.text: Nikharta Roop uses three channels for notifications. WhatsApp is the primary channel
as it has the highest open rate in India (95%+). SMS is the fallback. Email is used
only for receipts and admin reports.
OTP delivery, booking alerts when no WhatsApp
Payment receipts, monthly summary, admin reports
Real-time booking updates when app is installed
'नमस्ते [Name]! आपकी बुकिंग [Service] के लिए [Date] [Time] पर confirmed है। ID:
'आपकी बुकिंग confirm हो गई है। हम आपका इंतज़ार कर रहे हैं! 🌸'
'याद दिलाना: आपकी [Service] की अपॉइंटमेंट आज [Time] बजे है। निखरता रूप, [Address]'
'आपकी बुकिंग cancel हो गई। Refund 5-7 business days में आएगा।'
'खेद है! आपकी [Date] की बुकिंग cancel हो गई। कारण: [Reason]. दोबारा book करें।'
'सेवा पूरी हुई! आपका अनुभव कैसा रहा? Review करें: [link]'
'🎉 खुशखबरी! दिवाली पर 20% छूट। Code: DIWALI20. [Book Now Link]'
'[OTP] - यह आपका Nikharta Roop verification code है। किसी के साथ share न करें।'
'बधाई हो! आपने 500 loyalty points कमाए। अगली बुकिंग पर ₹100 की छूट मिलेगी।'
'हम आपको miss कर रहे थे! आपकी [Date] की appointment missed हो गई। दोबारा book करें।'
• A dedicated Notification Service (microservice or module) handles all outgoing
• The main API never directly calls SMS/WhatsApp — it enqueues a job in a message
• The Notification Service processes jobs from the queue — retries up to 3 times on
• All notifications are logged in a Notifications table with status (SENT / FAILED)
• Admin dashboard shows delivery stats: 95% WhatsApp delivery rate expected.
⚠️ Edge Case: If WhatsApp delivery fails (user hasn't opted in or number invalid), the
system automatically falls back to SMS for the same message within 30 seconds.

g.text: From Day 1, the database is designed with a branch_id on every major table. This
allows Nikharta Roop to expand to multiple cities without any schema changes.
Each city/location has its own branch_id; all in same DB
City admin sees only their branch; Super Admin sees all
All services are for one branch
Each branch can have different services and prices
All staff belong to one branch
Staff assigned to specific branches; transfers possible
Razorpay UPI — most popular in India; zero transaction fee for users
Razorpay Cards — credit/debit cards for higher-value bookings
Razorpay Net Banking — for customers without UPI
Razorpay captures 20% advance at booking; balance collected at parlour
Razorpay Refund API — triggered automatically on cancellation by admin
Razorpay sends webhook on payment success → backend updates booking to CONFIRMED
Next.js SSR + static generation for services page
Redis cache services list — TTL 1 hour
90% reduction in DB load for service queries
Cloudinary CDN + WebP format + lazy loading
Pre-compute slot availability on booking write (not read)
Proper indexes on booking_date, user_id, status
Horizontal scaling: add more API server instances behind load balancer
Builds trust and drives bookings from new users
Higher ticket value — bridal party packages
Each franchisee gets their own admin panel
Users upload selfie, get service recommendations

server without storing session on the server.
One-Time Password — a 6-digit code sent via SMS for secure, passwordless login.
An in-memory database used for fast temporary storage — used for OTPs, caches, and
A standard way for the frontend and backend to communicate using HTTP methods (GET,
A powerful open-source relational database that stores all business data.
Role-Based Access Control — a system where each user's role determines what actions
Server-Side Rendering — Next.js renders the page on the server before sending to the
browser, improving SEO and load speed.
Incremental Static Regeneration — Next.js regenerates static pages in the background
Content Delivery Network — serves files (images, JS) from servers closest to the user,
A URL that Razorpay or other services call automatically when an event (like payment
Firebase Cloud Messaging — Google's service for sending push notifications to Android
India's most popular payment gateway — supports UPI, cards, net banking, and wallets.
An Indian SMS service provider used for OTP delivery with high delivery rates in
Largest Contentful Paint — measures how quickly the main visible content of a web page
Cumulative Layout Shift — measures visual stability (elements not jumping around on
Instead of actually deleting a database record, setting is_active = false. Preserves
When two users try to do the same thing at the same time — e.g., booking the same slot
